skill.name: security-compliance
skill.description: Guides security teams through architecture reviews, compliance mapping, threat modeling, risk assessment, vulnerability prioritization, and incident response planning.
skill.summary: Practical security and compliance guidance with reusable frameworks, templates, and local risk tools.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from defensive prose, Markdown fences, sample data, and clearly labeled security examples. Confirmed issues include unsafe privileged PowerShell examples, a hardcoded JWT secret, a shared bulk-reset password, and unprotected identity evidence. No prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: The API example hardcodes a predictable Flask JWT secret.
remediation.suggestion: Load a high-entropy secret from an approved secret manager, fail when it is missing, and document rotation without exposing the value.

remediation.issue: The bulk account reset assigns one weak plaintext password to every matching user.
remediation.suggestion: Use per-user recovery flows or unique random temporary credentials. Add dry-run output, narrow targeting, approval, and forced reset controls.

remediation.issue: Privileged examples can reboot hosts, purge tenant email, change passwords, and revoke sessions.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit authorization, scope validation, dry-run, confirmation, rollback, and production change-control steps before each command.

remediation.issue: The MFA evidence example stores employee identity and authentication-factor metadata in plaintext.
remediation.suggestion: Collect only required fields, use restrictive permissions and encryption, redact shared outputs, and define approved storage and retention.

semantic_findings.title: Bulk Password Reset Uses a Shared Plaintext Credential
semantic_findings.description: The incident-response example assigns every matching user the same plaintext password, TempPassword123!, during a bulk reset. This enables predictable credential reuse and broad account compromise.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command directly sets one literal password for every user returned by an all-users query. The insecure credential and broad scope are explicit.

semantic_findings.title: MFA Evidence Example Stores Detailed Identity Data Without Protection
semantic_findings.description: The SOC 2 example writes user identifiers, email addresses, MFA enrollment status, and factor types to JSON without access controls, encryption, or data minimization guidance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The collected fields and plaintext JSON write are explicit. The example provides no file-permission, encryption, redaction, or retention safeguards around this identity evidence.

high_findings.title: Generic API/secret keys

content.value_statement: Security teams often need consistent methods for risk, controls, and incident response. This skill provides practical frameworks, templates, and local assessment tools.
actual_capabilities: Maps security controls to SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA, and PCI DSS requirements.
Builds qualitative and quantitative risk assessments, including SLE, ALE, risk levels, and control cost analysis.
Prioritizes CSV vulnerability records using CVSS, asset criticality, exposure, exploit activity, data sensitivity, and compensating controls.
Structures threat models with STRIDE, attack trees, MITRE ATT&CK mappings, and documented mitigations.
Provides incident classification, response workflows, tabletop exercises, playbooks, and post-incident report templates.
Reviews application, cloud, identity, network, and DevSecOps designs against established security practices.
limitations: The guidance does not replace qualified auditors, legal counsel, privacy specialists, or regulatory authorities.
Framework mappings and deadlines require validation against current standards, contracts, jurisdictions, and organizational scope.
The bundled scripts process local CSV data. They do not discover assets, scan systems, or validate vulnerabilities.
Operational examples can change live systems. Test them in a controlled environment and require explicit authorization.

use_cases.title: Design a Security Architecture
use_cases.description: Create layered controls, trust boundaries, identity requirements, logging coverage, and a prioritized implementation roadmap.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Compliance Program
use_cases.description: Map requirements to controls, identify evidence, assign owners, record gaps, and plan audit readiness activities.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Security Operations
use_cases.description: Classify incidents, rank vulnerabilities, define response deadlines, and produce concise reports for technical and executive teams.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Risk Register
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a risk register for [organization]. Use these assets, threats, and controls: [details]. Score likelihood and impact, then recommend owners and actions.

prompt_templates.title: Map Controls to SOC 2
prompt_templates.prompt: Map these controls to relevant SOC 2 criteria: [controls]. Identify evidence, control owners, testing frequency, gaps, and practical remediation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Incident Response Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop an incident response plan for [scenario]. Define severity, roles, containment decisions, evidence handling, recovery checks, communications, and post-incident actions.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Architecture and Quantify Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this architecture: [details]. Create trust boundaries and threats, estimate SLE and ALE, map controls, evaluate residual risk, and prioritize investments.

output_examples.input: Assess ransomware risk for a production service valued at $5 million with a 20 percent annual occurrence rate.
output: Risk: Critical. Estimated annual loss exposure is $600,000, based on a 60 percent exposure factor.
Priority controls: immutable backups, endpoint detection, network segmentation, privileged access controls, and tested recovery procedures.
Residual risk requires owner approval after control costs and recovery targets are validated.

output_examples.input: Prepare a SOC 2 access control evidence plan for a SaaS company using Okta and AWS.
output: Control objective: production access requires approval, least privilege, MFA, and quarterly certification.
Evidence: Okta enrollment reports, AWS access records, approval tickets, termination samples, and review sign-offs.
Testing: sample users quarterly, document exceptions, protect collected identity data, and retain only required evidence.

output_examples.input: Create first-hour actions for a confirmed credential compromise affecting a production administrator.
output: Classify the incident, assign an incident commander, preserve relevant logs, and confirm the affected identities and systems.
Revoke active sessions and credentials through approved procedures, then monitor for persistence and lateral movement.
Record every action, notify required stakeholders, and define recovery checks before restoring access.

best_practices: Provide business context, system boundaries, data sensitivity, existing controls, and evidence quality with every assessment.
Validate framework versions, legal duties, and risk assumptions with accountable specialists before making final decisions.
Test scripts and administrative commands in isolated environments, use least privilege, and review planned changes before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a compliance checklist as proof that systems are secure.
Do not run sample commands against production systems without authorization, scoping, backups, and change approval.
Do not place real secrets, personal data, internal addresses, or unredacted evidence in prompts or sample files.

faq.question: Which compliance frameworks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, NIST CSF, CIS Controls, and related security practices.

faq.question: Can this skill certify an organization?
faq.answer: No. Certification and attestation require qualified auditors or assessors, complete evidence, defined scope, and formal review.

faq.question: Does the skill scan networks or applications?
faq.answer: No. The bundled scripts calculate risk and vulnerability priority from supplied local CSV files.

faq.question: Can I use the incident response content during an active incident?
faq.answer: Yes, as a planning reference. Follow approved playbooks, preserve evidence, involve authorized responders, and meet legal notification duties.

faq.question: How should I handle sensitive evidence?
faq.answer: Minimize collected fields, restrict access, encrypt storage and transport, define retention, redact outputs, and use approved evidence repositories.

faq.question: Are the sample commands ready for production?
faq.answer: No. Replace placeholders, verify scope and permissions, test safely, review destructive effects, and obtain change approval before execution.
